definition: Reclusive means living in deliberate solitude, avoiding the company of others.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word reclusive. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know reclusive should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The reclusive game designer skipped his own launch party, streaming a brief thank-you from his cabin instead.
Private is weaker than reclusive: a private person simply keeps personal matters to themselves, while a reclusive one avoids human company itself.
Hermitic is stronger than reclusive — a hermitic life is organized entirely around total isolation, while a reclusive person may still tolerate the occasional distant wave.

Solitary states the neutral fact of being alone, whether chosen or not — a solitary lighthouse keeper may wish for visitors who never come. Reclusive adds the deliberate choice: a reclusive person arranges life on purpose to avoid the company of others.

Withdrawn describes a pulling back that is often temporary and emotional — someone quiet and unreachable after a loss, frequently while still living among people. Reclusive is a settled way of life: deliberately organizing existence to keep human company away altogether.

Fans of the puzzle column knew their setter only as 'Quill.' Quill declined every interview, sent a lawyer to accept awards, and had prize checks mailed to a forwarding service.

When a journalist finally traced the byline to a farmhouse at the end of a private road, the neighbors could only report that the owner bought feed in the next county and waved from a distance, maybe once a year.
Quill was not hiding anything, they insisted — just deeply, contentedly reclusive.
Quill refuses interviews, ceremonies, and even neighborly contact by choice — with no wrongdoing involved — which is the deliberate solitude that reclusive names.
neutral; descriptive rather than judgmental
Reclusive involves no secrecy or scheming at all — it simply means avoiding company.
Contrast this unit's connive (secretly plotting with others) and furtive (acting in a sneaky, guilty-seeming manner): a reclusive person may be perfectly open about wanting to be left alone.

For a decade, the proof was the most famous unfinished business in mathematics — and then Ana Petrov posted it online, complete, with no announcement.
Prize committees tried to reach her.
Journalists flew to her hometown.
The university offered a chair with no teaching duties at all.
Every letter went unanswered.
Petrov, colleagues explained, had become genuinely reclusive: she had moved to her grandmother's farmhouse, kept no phone, and turned her life deliberately away from other people.
It was not shyness about the work, a former classmate insisted, and it was not a snub.
She simply built her days so that no one could reach them.
The proof still answers every question mathematicians put to it.
